newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Oct 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
The National People's Congress, or parliament, ends its session with the passage of laws on township enterprises, noise pollution and civil air defence.
Premier Li Peng says Japan should follow the path of peaceful development and reiterates Beijing's stance that the Diaoyu islands are Chinese territory.
A commentary urges European leaders not to play the part of trumpet for the Dalai Lama and hints that the Tibet issue could harm Sino-European relations.
Central bank governor Dai Xianglong says China's broad M2 money supply grew by a year-on-year 26 percent at in January to September while M1 money supply grew by 15 percent during the period.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission orders commodity futures exchanges to abolish a settlement system that sets limits on the total amount for physical delivery.
China will issue 1.0 billion yuan in bonds for the Three Gorges dam project on the Yangtze river. A portion of the bonds will likely be issued abroad.
